hero.title: Echoes of the Witch Wood
hero.sub: A solid and scalable action-platformer architecture, built on custom C++ systems and modular AI logic.
hero.img_alt: Architectural diagram of gameplay interfaces and subsystems
hero.img1_desc: Decoupled architecture overview: AHeroCharacter interfaces with Save, Environmental, and AI subsystems strictly via abstraction contracts (ISaveGameInterface and IFloorInterface), eliminating hard casting and circular dependencies.
hero.img2_desc: Save System persistence pipeline: data propagation flow from in-world triggers (ACheckpoint) down to local disk storage via UEchoesSaveData, separating player progression and slot metadata.

text: Originally conceived as a cross-functional indie initiative—bringing together graduates from different tracks like programming, concept art, and 3D modeling—this project was a great exercise in remote team-building via Discord and core systems architecture.
Although the team eventually parted ways and development was suspended, the C++ code produced for the AI and save systems remains some of my most structured and educational work.

concept.title: Systems over Quantity
desc: The focus was on creating a robust framework for a two-character platformer.
Every system was designed to be actor-agnostic:
from portals to moving platforms, communication occurs via interfaces to ensure maximum maintainability.

points.1: AI & Enemy Framework: Developed a generic enemy base class with health management and a complex 'Kamikaze' AI, complete with State Machines (Chase, Attack, Stroll), Behavior Trees (Blackboard), and positional SFX.
points.2: Save Architecture: Implementation of a complete data persistence pipeline based on interfaces, supporting checkpoints, multiple slots, and serialization of Player State and Game State.
points.3: Advanced Movement Systems: Development of the Dash mechanic (Ground/Air) with conflict resolution on steep surfaces, and creation of a 'Floor Checking' system through C++ components and interfaces.
points.4: Environmental Mechanics: Design of Spline-based moving platforms, timed platforms (falling platforms), and a portal system for instantaneous actor teleportation.
points.5: Modular Audio System: Creation of a custom audio component to standardize sound variable management and simplify playback functions across the project.

lessons.title: Lessons Learned
desc: Through this project, I refined C++ Timer management for timed mechanics and Inheritance logic for AI.
Code cleanliness and the creation of a CodeMap were vital for coordinating movement systems with interaction systems (levers/doors).
